To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the terminal complement complex C5b- 9 can be quantitated by ELISA, that it is present in normal and atherosclerotically involved arterial walls, and that it is increased in atherosclerotical lesions.

a quantitative ELISA for the terminal C5-9 complement complex, using a monoclonal antibody against neoantigents, has been used to demonstrate the presence of terminal C5b 9 complexes in atherosclerictic lesions.
the plasma concentration of SC 5b-9 is in the range of the levels of the same complex eluted from the atherosclerotics arteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a quantitative ELISA to measure the terminal C5-9 complement complex in human atherosclerosis.
the role of the complement system in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
the role of complement in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atherosclerosis is associated with complement activation, and this is a consequence of the disease, and not its cause.
the terminal complement complex is present in atherosclerosis and that the levels of C5-9 are elevated in atherosclerotics.

C5b-8 and C5b-7 are present in atherosclerotics and that the presence of these neoantigens in the arterial wall is related to the presence of C5b, C6, and C8, and the absence of C9, which is the last component of the terminal complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
complement activation occurs in atherosclerotics and the terminal complex is formed in atherosclertic arteries.
complement activation is a significant component of the atherogenesis process.

the C5b-7 and C5b-8 complexes, as well as the C5b complex, were present at higher concentration in the atherosclerotisic plaques and in the normal and fatty streak intima and media than in normal arteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C5b-8 complex is a major component of the C5b9 complex, which is the most abundant component in atherosclerosis.
the complement system is activated in atherosclerosis, and that the complement system may be a potential target for treatment of the disease.
the complement system plays a role in the progression of atherosclerosis.
